angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 660,915 km at 196.19 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 5.0970 +/- 0.0318 mas (same row, RUWE 1.53): 196.19 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published
radiusSource: Radius 0.95 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of K2-158 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract): 660,915 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.92 +/- 0.03 solar masses from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of K2-158 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5503 +/- 51 K from Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-158 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Livingston et al. 2018, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of K2-158 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/k2-158.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.446, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-158 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.07 dex, from Livingston et al. 2018 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018AJ....156...78L/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of K2-158 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.16298, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: Gaia DR3 FLAME (Creevey et al. 2023, A&A 674, A26), astrophysical_parameters of Gaia DR3 3596003497911958528, flags_flame 00: age_flame 11.351515 Gyr (16th to 84th percentiles 9.681263 to 13.1261015)

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from a blackbody at the star's published temperature (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
